1.  The present DAR arises out of road accident in which one Deepak Das, aged about 18 years, suffered injuries. In terms of the provision of Motor Vehicle Act, the same is treated as a claim petition.

1 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 07.11.2021, upon receipt of information through DD no. 41A regarding flipping of a vehicle near Khanna Market, Lodhi Road,
investigating officer reached the spot where one vehicle Eicher Tempo bearing no.
DL-1LAE-4509 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) was found flipped on the middle of the road. The person injured had been taken to the hospital by then. On reaching the hospital, one of the injured Ganesh Das stated that on 07.11.2021 at 03:00 p.m., he was travelling along with 12 other people in the offending vehicle. After performing religious ritual (idol immersion) near Yamuna River, at Sarai Kale Khan, all the 13 passengers boarded the offending vehicle for returning to Bengali Camp. When the offending tempo reached near Najaf Khan Tomb at Najaf Khan Road,
Lodhi Road, the driver of the offending vehicle /respondent no.1 started driving the vehicle at CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date:

causing injury to its passengers and death of the son of one of the petitioners. 
3. An FIR No. 206/2021 dated 07.11.2021 u/s 188/279/269/337/338/304A of IPC &
Section 3 Epidemic Disease Act was registered at PS Lodhi Colony. Police investigated the matter and filed chargesheet before concerned Criminal Court and DAR was filed before this Tribunal.
4. As per record, the offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1, is owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no.3. In response to the DAR,
insurance company filed its reply denying its liability to compensate the petitioner on the ground that the offending vehicle was being plied in violation of the permit as per which the offending vehicle was only allowed to be use as a light goods carriage vehicle. It is further pleaded that even the injured Deepak Das was found to be under influence of alcohol. It is pleaded that since the offending vehicle could be used only as a light goods carriage vehicle, petitioner was an unauthorized /gratuitous passenger along with 12 other persons, all of whom were in violation of the Covid-19 pandemic (DDMA guidelines) guidelines and thus not entitled to compensation. It is further pleaded that there is a possibility that the offending vehicle may have been planted to raise a false claim. It is however not denied that the offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent no.3 vide policy no.
CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2024.10.21 04:03:54 +0530 MACT No. 328/22 Deepak Das vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 3 of 25(ss) RL2012070054 for the period from 07.12.2020 to 06.12.2021. 
Despite opportunity, no reply was filed on behalf of respondent no.1 or respondent no.2.
5. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 17.01.2023.

2 1) Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 07.11.2021 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL-1AE-4509 (Eicher Canter) being driven by R1, owned by R-2 and insured with R3? OPP. 
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom ? OPP.
3) Relief. 
6. In order to prove his claim, petitioner/Deepak Das examined himself as PW-1. He relied upon his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A wherein he reiterated the factum and manner of the accident. He deposed that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1. He further relied upon his MLC prepared at AIIMS Trauma Center as de exhibited and marked as Mark A, original discharge summary as Ex.PW1/2, his medical bills as Ex.PW1/3(colly), his Adhar Card as Ex.PW1/4 and his PAN card as Ex.PW1/5. He deposed that on account of being bedridden for about 1 month due to the accident, he had to incur medical expenditure of Rs.5,000/-,
Rs.10,000/- towards special diet and Rs.15,000/- towards conveyance. He deposed that at the time of the accident he was 18 years of age and was doing a private job in Delhi and earning Rs.16,000/-
to 18,000/- per month. Due to the accident, he lost his job and earnings. PW-1 was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for respondent no.1 and 2 and cross examined by Ld . Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2024.10.21 04:04:00 +0530 MACT No. 328/22 Deepak Das vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 4 of 25(ss) Counsel for 3/insurance company. 
7. Upon closing of petitioner evidence, respondent no.1 led his evidence by examining himself as RW1. 
RW1 Akendra Kumar led his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.R1W1/A. In his affidavit, he has stated that the offending vehicle was not involved in the alleged accident. He denied any rash or negligent act on his part in driving of the offending vehicle. He stated that the petitioner/victims have falsely implicated him and that FIR no. 206/21 has been lodged with a motive to extort money from the respondents. He stated that none of the alleged victims were travelling in the offending vehicle. He relied upon his identity card as Ex.R1W1/1. He was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for insurance company. Such cross examination was adopted by ld. Counsel for petitioners. 
8. In respondent evidence, the owner of the offending vehicle /respondent no.2 also examined himself as RW2/Sh. Bhanu Prakash Sharma. He led his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.R2WA and his identity card as Ex.R2W2/1. RW2 also denied involvement of the offending vehicle in the alleged accident and pleaded the FIR to be false and concocted. He asserted that the liability to pay compensation, if any, lies upon the insurance company with which his vehicle was insured. 
9. Insurance company /respondent no.3 also examined its witness Sh. Parth Arya as R3W1. R3W1 led his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.R3W1/1 wherein he testified that as per the Registration Certificate, the offending vehicle was a light goods Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2024.10.21 04:04:04 +0530 MACT No. 328/22 Deepak Das vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page Deepak Das (Dar) vs Akendra Kumar(206/21,Lc) on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157081334/
3 no. 5 of 25(ss) vehicle with a seating capacity of 3 persons. He stated that the said vehicle was being used for transportation of passengers, beyond its permitted capacity, in violation of the permit. He testified that since the respondent no.1 and 2 committed breach of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy by violating the RC and permit, the insurance company is not liable to compensate the petitioners. He relied upon his authority letter as Ex.R3W1/1, attested copy of the insurance policy as Ex.R3W1/3 and DAR /FIR /chargesheet/RC/Route Permit as already Ex.PW1/6 (colly). He was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for respondent no.1 and 2.
10. Final arguments in detail were addressed by learned counsel for the petitioners/victims and counsel for all the respondents. 
It has been argued on behalf of the petitioners that since that son of petitioner no.1 lost his life in the accident that is proved to have occurred due to rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1,
respondent no.3, with which the offending vehicle was insured may be directed to compensate the petitioners. On the other hand, it is argued by respondent no.1 and 2 that the petitioners have failed to prove rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1 or the involvement of the vehicle in the alleged accident. It is further argued that even if the accident is assumed to be proved, it is respondent no.3 which is liable to compensate the petitioners. It is argued on behalf of respondent no.3 that the petitioner/victims were traveling in the offending vehicle as unauthorized and gratuitous passengers since the GUPTA Date: 2024.10.21 MACT No. 328/22 Deepak Das vs.
Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 6 of 25(ss) +0530 offending vehicle was a goods carriage vehicle. It is argued that the offending vehicle was insured as a goods carriage vehicle and could not carry any passenger except for the driver and owner of the goods. It is further argued that the insured i.e.
respondent no.2 has further violated the condition of RC which permitted a maximum of 3 persons to be seated in the offending vehicle. It is argued that as there is a clear breach of the terms and condition of the insurance policy, insurance company is not liable to compensate the victims. 
Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 07.11.2021 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL-1AE-4509 (Eicher Canter) being driven by R1, owned by R-2 and insured with R3? OPP. 
11. Before proceeding to decide the above issue, it is apposite to note that as a settled principle of law, proceedings under The Motor Vehicle Act are not considered akin to the proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not applicable. Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs.
Amir Chand & ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. 
 Digitally  signed by  CHARU  CHARU GUPTA  GUPTA Date:

4  +0530 MACT No. 328/22 Deepak Das vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 7 of 25(ss)
12. In the present case, the injured /petitioner has specifically deposed about accident dated 07.11.2021. He has categorically stated that at the time of the accident, offending vehicle bearing no.
DL-1LAE-4509 was being driven by respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner. He has deposed that the driver of the offending vehicle deliberately ignored the warnings to be slow and careful. It is due to his rash and negligent driving that the offending vehicle overturned with the sudden and forceful impact causing injuries to its passengers and death of one of them. 
13. In the present case, the Tribunal takes judicial notice of the fact that a common evidence has been recorded by one single Local Commissioner in all the 13 connected matters. It is a matter of record that injured victims namely Vishal Majumdar, Debu Das, Ganesh Dass and Vidhan Biswas have also been examined as eye witnesses /victims in all the cases. Apart from the testimony of the petitioner, testimony of other victims regarding the factum of accident, manner of accident, rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1, is coherent and suffers from no apparent discrepancy. All the victims have corroborated that despite being repeatedly cautioned, driver of the offending vehicle continued to drive at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and lost control/balance while taking a sharp turn. 
Though the respondents have denied that the offending vehicle was hired by Ganesh Das or anyone else for the purpose of idol immersion, reporting of the matter immediately to the police on the same date sizure of the vehicle by the police on the same date, preparation of MLCs of the victims as well as Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 04:04:18 Date: 2024.10.21 +0530 MACT No. 328/22 Deepak Das vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 8 of 25(ss) respondent no.1 at the same time and in the same hospital as well as filing of chargesheet by the investigating officer after thorough investigation of the accident, supports the plea of the petitioners. It has been held in National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi that the completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 
It is further observed that though respondent no.1 and 2 denied occurrence of the accident in their evidence as R1W1 and R2W1 respectively, during cross examination of R1W1 (i.e. respondent no.1/driver), such witness admitted being driver of the offending vehicle on the date of accident. 
Though he volunteered to state that he was not driving the said vehicle at the time of the alleged accident, he admitted that at around 02:00 p.m he took the vehicle from Lodhi Road Bus Stand and was going towards Chhatarpur. On further cross-examination he stated that he was not injured in the said accident, but on the contrary, also admitted that his medical record of treatment was prepared at AIIMS Hospital on the date of accident. The admission on the part of respondent no.1 regarding being driver of the offending vehicle at the relevant time and the fact that he was taken to AIIMS Hospital for treatment on the date of accident, proves the factum of occurrence of the accident. Since no evidence has been led by the respondents to show that respondent no.1 was not driving the offending vehicle rashly or negligently, by preponderance of probabilities, claim of the victims that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1, stands proved. by CHARU CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date:

Page no. 9 of 25(ss) It has also been pleaded on behalf of the insurance company that since the victim was under the influence of alcohol and was out on the streets in violation of the Covid-19 Pandemic guidelines, deduction in respect of contributory negligence also be made. There is nothing in the MLC of the petitioner to show that he was intoxicated. In the considered opinion of this Tribunal, intoxication by the victim (mere passenger in a vehicle) or breach of pandemic protocol issued only for safety from the pandemic, are not grounds that contributed to the occurrence to the accident and hence no deduction qua contributory negligence is permissible.
14. In totality of circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioners have been able to prove at the scales of preponderance of probabilities that the accident in question, took place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing no. DL-1LAE-4509 by its driver/respondent no.1 on the date and time of accident. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioners/claimants and against the respondents. 
Issue no. 2 Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom? OPP. 
15. As regards the issue of liability of the respondents, respondent no.3 has raised a statutory defence pleading that the offending vehicle was being plied in breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy in as much as the offending vehicle held RC as a goods carriage vehicle and was not CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2024.10.21 04:04:29 +0530 MACT No. 328/22 Deepak Das vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 10 of 25(ss) permitted to carry victims as passengers. It is further pleaded that since the son of the petitioner no.1 and all other injured victims were mere gratuitous passengers travelling in the offending vehicle without authorization, insurance company is not liable to compensate them. 
In order to establish this defence, respondent no.3 has examined Sh. Parth Arya, Deputy Manger (legal claims) as R3W1. R3W1 has duly proved the terms and conditions of the insurance policy which clearly do not cover the use of offending vehicle as a passenger vehicle. Since it stands proved in issue no.1 that the offending vehicle was carrying the victims as gratuitous passengers, there is certainly a breach of the terms and conditions of insurance policy. 
Now, whether the payment of compensation is to made jointly by the owner and driver of the vehicle or by the insurer which could thereafter be recovered by the owner and driver, has to be considered in the light of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Anu Bhanvara vs. IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Company AIR 2019 SC 3934. In the said judgment, Apex Court held that the insurance of the vehicle, though as a goods vehicle, is not disputed by the parties. It held that since the claimants were young children who suffered permanent disability on account of the injuries sustained in the accident, the principle of "pay and recover" should be directed to be invoked in the present case. The court accordingly held that the insurance company shall have right to realize the compensation amount from the driver and owner of the vehicle in accordance with the law.

16 . As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 
This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 
17. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary damages (Special damages)

17.1. In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a)
and (iv). 17.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii),

17.3. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and under Item (ii) (a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the evidence. 
17.4. Award under the head of future medical expenses--Item (iii)--depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof.

18. As per record Adhar Card of petitioner Ex.PW1/4 and his PAN Card Ex.PW1/5, proves his date of birth as 08.02.2003. Same has not been disputed. Accident occurred on 07.11.2021. As such,
petitioner would have been about 18 years at the time of accident. 
19. As per MLC Ex.PW1/1, injured suffered abrasion over forehead of 2cm approximately, multiple abrasion over right elbow and right hand measuring 1cmX2cm. He was discharged on the same day and his injury was opined to be simple in nature. 
Thus, keeping note of the nature of injury suffered by the petitioner, he did not suffer from any loss of income on account of the injury.

The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

No compensation towards future loss of income can be granted in cases where petitioner has not proved to have sustained any permanent disability.
In the case of semi-illiterate claimants,
the Tribunal should ordinarily invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit.
, the Tribunal can release the whole or part of the amount of compensation to the claimant provided the Tribunal will ensure that the amount is invested for the purpose for which it is demanded and paid.

The expression used in guideline No. (iv) issued by this Court is that in the case of literate persons also the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i), whereas in the guideline Nos.
(i), (ii), (iii) and (v), the expression used is that the Tribunal should.
Moreover, in the case of literate persons, the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i) only if, having regard to the age, fiscal background and strata of the society to which the claimant belongs and such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks that in the larger interest of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded, it is necessary to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit.

Thus, sufficient discretion has been given to the Tribunal not to insist on investment of the compensation amount in long term fixed deposit and to release even the whole amount in the case of literate persons.
The guidelines were not to be understood to mean that the Tribunals were to take a rigid stand while considering an application seeking release of the money.

The guidelines cast a responsibility on the Tribunals to pass appropriate orders after examining each case on its own merits.
However, it is seen that even in cases when there is no possibility or chance of the feed being frittered away by the beneficiary owing to ignorance, illiteracy or susceptibility to exploitation, investment of the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit is directed by the Tribunals as a matter of course and in a routine manner, ignoring the object and the spirit of the guidelines issued by this Court and the genuine requirements of the claimants.
Even in the case of literate persons, the Tribunals are automatically ordering investment of the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit without recording that having regard to the age or fiscal background or the strata of the society to which the claimant belongs or such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks it necessary to direct such investment in the larger interests of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded to him.

The Tribunals very often dispose of the claimant's application for withdrawal of the amount of compensation in a mechanical manner and without proper application of mind.
This has resulted in serious injustice and hardship to the claimants.
